hub.layout: body padding-right 10px + hidden root scrollbar (the source scrolls inside a 10px-gutter viewport)

auth.noChromeMechanism: scripts/scripts.js NO_CHROME_TEMPLATES = ['auth']: loadEager removes body > header and body > footer after decorateTemplateAndTheme(), loadLazy skips loadHeader/loadFooter; styles.css also hides body.auth > header/footer so no 90px reservation paints

sectionScaffold: main > .section margin 0; main > .section > div max-width none, margin 0, padding 0 - blocks own their wraps and gutters; no content cap at foundation level (R-02: hub fluid, sign-in 370px module cap lives in the auth-login block)
baseTypography: browser defaults (the prototypes reset nothing but box-sizing); body 16px/24px, color #000, font var(--font-light) on hub
imgReset: img, video { display: block; max-width: 100% } img { height: auto }
navHeight: --nav-height: 90px at every width; header background var(--hub-red)

chrome.header: blocks/header - /nav: section 1 linked logo img (alt 'Go to IF-Hub'), section 2 <ul> of links, section 3 search placeholder text; burger + red drawer below 768px; search overlay over /query-index.json
chrome.footer:
blocks/footer - /footer: section 1
    links + copyright

    , section 2 the login shortcut link (renders the fixed red lock button .hub-login bottom-left)

notes: The hub login shortcut (.hub-login) is rendered by the footer block - page blocks must not build it.
blocks/cards, blocks/hero, blocks/columns are stock boilerplate blocks; a page block named 'cards' replaces the stock one - rename (e.g. hub-cards) or overwrite deliberately.
Do not emit <header> elements inside block DOM (the header reservation rule matches every <header>).
